programme.title: Life on Earth
programme.desc: The story of life, from the first primitive cells to the plants and animals that now live around us. David Attenborough examines the uses and advantages of birds' unique possession - the feather. Man has yet to invent anything that, weight for weight, is as strong as the feather. Feathers are insulators, they provide the surface of the most perfect aerofoils known - bird's wings. Plus they play a central role in courtship.

programme.title: Gloria: My Life on TV
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford looks back at her extraordinary career and reveals what it has been like to be woman, mother and grandmother on television and radio for more than half a century.

programme.title: Gloria Hunniford Remembers... Doris Day
programme.desc: In the 1950s and 60s, Doris Day ranked amongst cinema’s biggest box office stars, thanks to roles in films such as musical Calamity Jane, Hitchcock’s The Man Who Knew Too Much, and especially a string of hit romantic comedies, including the classic Pillow Talk. Amongst the movie icon’s millions of fans across the world was a young Gloria Hunniford, who in 1995, years after Doris had unexpectedly stepped back from Hollywood and swapped fame for anonymity, was invited to Doris’s home in Carmel, USA, for an exclusive opportunity to interview her heroine. Here, ahead of a special screening of that rare interview, Gloria draws back the curtain on her encounter with one of cinema’s great female idols and shares her memories of how the meeting came together, and the special behind-the-scenes moments that TV viewers of the day never got to see.

programme.title: Doris Day: Pebble Mill Special
programme.desc: Gloria Hunniford travels to Carmel, USA for an exclusive interview with Hollywood star Doris Day. First broadcast in January 1995.

programme.desc: The story of life, from the first primitive cells to the plants and animals that now live around us. Feathers are insulators, they provide the surface of the most perfect aerofoils known - bird's wings. Plus they play a central role in courtship.

programme.title: Eisteddfod

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: More than 150 of the country's best young musicians take us on a metaphorical musical journey to the underworld and back under the watchful eye of conductor and composer Thomas Adès. Always a hotly anticipated highlight of any BBC Proms season, the National Youth Orchestra is at the Royal Albert Hall with a programme that opens with Liszt's intoxicating Mephisto Waltz No 1, a whirlwind score following the Faust legend as he waltzes out into the forest with a local village girl. Next up is a rare treat of a new piece conducted by the composer himself: Purgatorio–Dante ballet Part II is Thomas Adès’s contemplation of purgatory in this central act of his Grammy Award-winning ballet. To round off the concert, the orchestra delivers the dazzling Symphonie Fantastique by Berlioz. A vast young orchestra drenches the Royal Albert Hall in this mesmerising symphony. Presented by Petroc Trelawny.

programme.title: The Brontës Lived Here: Writers' Houses
programme.desc: Margaret Drabble visits Haworth Parsonage and the Yorkshire Moors, home of the famous literary family the Brontës and the setting for Emily's Wuthering Heights.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: It was at a 1975 production of his play The Birthday Party that Harold Pinter first met Lady Antonia Fraser and changed both their lives with the single phrase: 'Must you go?' What followed was a scandal that gripped London's high society and a marriage that lasted 28 years, until Pinter's death in 2008. Here, Lady Antonia explains how that original encounter has always meant that the play holds a special meaning for her, despite its unsettling nature - and she looks back fondly on the BBC's 1987 acclaimed adaptation of The Birthday Party and her husband's performance as the mysteriously menacing Goldberg, alongside a cast that includes Kenneth Cranham, Julie Walters and Dame Joan Plowright.

programme.title: The Birthday Party
programme.desc: It's Stanley's birthday, but the party that is thrown for him is not quite what he was expecting. Written by Harold Pinter.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Nigel Williams's two-part film biography explores Pinter's life, work, and political passions - from his East End childhood to his work as an actor, his experience of both early critical rejection and adulation, his screenwriting, and his love of poetry and passion for cricket. Part One explores Pinter's key theme - the room - through the very rooms in which he wrote his first great series of plays. Arena reveals the links between the plays and places, and meets the people who live there now. We visit the East London terraced house room where Pinter grew up and first wrote poetry; the theatre dressing room where he began to formulate his ideas about playwriting and language; the sitting room in the London cold-water flat where he wrote his first hit, The Caretaker, and his study in the bow-fronted house in Worthing, where he lived in the sixties with his first wife Vivien Merchant, and wrote The Homecoming. Harold Pinter has given Arena exclusive access to personal recordings in which he talks frankly to his biographer Michael Billington. Presented for the first time on television, they tell Pinter's story in his own words, as he remembers it.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: In part two of this film biography, Arena explores the relationship between the public and private dimensions of the famous playwright and actor's life and work; the intimacy of his plays since the seventies; his work in films and television drama; his passion for poetry; and his fervent 'political engagement'. Arena accompanied Pinter for two years to film plays and events in America and all over Europe. The wildly funny Celebration features a group of friends celebrating in a restaurant and, over the course of the evening, revealing details of their private lives in this very public space. Arena reunites members of the cast, including Lindsay Duncan, Andy de la Tour, Susan Wooldridge and Indira Varma, who discuss their working relationship with Harold Pinter. Other contributors include his wife Lady Antonia Fraser, journalist John Pilger and Pinter's biographer Michael Billington.

programme.title: The Architecture the Railways Built
programme.desc: Tim Dunn explores disused tube station Down Street in Mayfair, which played a crucial tactical role during WWII, and tours Rotterdam Centraal station with its designer.

programme.title: The Flying Gardener
programme.desc: Chris Beardshaw visits inspirational gardens by helicopter. A look at fine examples of vertical gardening found in the castles and villages of the Cotswolds, plus climbing plants.

programme.title: Art of Spain
programme.desc: Critic and art historian Andrew Graham-Dixon travels from southern to northern Spain to tell the story of some of Europe's most exciting and vital art. He journeys to the country’s scorched centre to explore Spanish art of the 16th and 17th centuries. From the mystical world of El Greco to the tender genius of Velazquez, this was a moment so extraordinary it became known as the Golden Age. But beneath the glittering surface was a dark and savage heart. Travelling from the architectural jewel of Toledo to majestic Madrid, Andrew Graham-Dixon traces the rise and fall of the Spanish Empire, the brutal conquest of the New World, and the religious madness of the Inquisition, to discover how a history so violent could produce some of the most beautiful art ever seen.

programme.title: Mastermind

programme.title: Call My Bluff

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox joins the team to explore the mind-bending mysteries of black holes discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope’s most exciting new observations.

programme.title: Omnibus
programme.desc: Humphrey Burton examines the golden age of Spanish painting, originally broadcast in 1976 to coincide with a major exhibition at the Royal Academy of Arts.

programme.title: One Hundred Great Paintings
programme.desc: Edwin Mullins looks at Francisco de Zurbaran's Still Life with Lemons, Oranges and a Rose.

programme.title: Britain's Lost Waterlands: Escape to Swallows and Amazons Country
programme.desc: Documentary that follows presenters Dick Strawbridge and Alice Roberts as they explore the spectacular British landscapes that inspired children's author Arthur Ransome to write his series Swallows and Amazons. The landscapes he depicted are based on three iconic British waterlands. The beauty and drama of the Lake District shaped by ancient glaciers and rich in wildlife and natural resources, the shallow man-made waterways of the Norfolk broads so crucial to farming and reed production, and the coastal estuaries and deep-water harbours of the Suffolk coastline shaped by ferocious tides and crucial to trade. Engineer and keen sailor Dick uses vintage boats to explore the landscapes and meet people whose lives are shaped by the water, while wildlife enthusiast Alice explores the rich shorelines, interrogating the underlying geography and meeting the wildlife. Together they evoke the nostalgia of Ransome's writing and a bygone era of childhood freedom and adventure, but they also explore the economic significance of these special locations and the ways in which water was harnessed to change the course of British history.

programme.desc: Clive heads to one of the Dominican Republic’s most northerly provinces, to the beautiful city of Puerto Plata. programme.title: The Big Cases
programme.desc: The chilling story of Hull’s funeral home horror. How an undertaker drowning in debt betrayed hundreds of grieving families. Robert Bush hoarded bodies, sold fake funeral plans and presented families with the ashes of strangers. His shocking crimes went undetected for years. The discovery led to one of the most complex investigations in Humberside Police’s history, with help from the National Crime Agency. At the heart of this are grieving families. In their darkest days, they fought for laws to regulate the funeral industry so that others never suffer their pain - or guilt - again.

programme.title: The Climate Question
programme.desc: A global programme that reflects the variety of takes on climate change, how best to understand it and the world's attempts to avert it, temper it or adapt to it. It is not about questioning whether climate change is happening, it's about finding the best ways to respond to it. This is sharp-edged, analytical inquiry. Hard scrutiny, touched with a sense of adventure and discovery, and where we can find it, hope. It includes stories from across the world on why we find it so hard to save our own planet, and how we might change that.

programme.title: The Travel Show
programme.desc: The traditional French bistro is mounting a comeback. In recent times, an average of 25 a day have been shutting their doors, as eating habits change across France. Now though, efforts are underway to save them. Briony May Williams travels through the south of the country to find out what this casual form of dining has brought to French culture. She heads to a village that's finally about to reopen a bistro that it lost many years ago, and explores the rowdy breakfast culture of Lyon's Machon cafes.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Can oil really save Venezuela’s economy? The country has the world’s largest reserves, so can it take advantage whilst global energy supplies are under pressure because of events in the Middle East? Reviving Venezuela’s biggest industry is just one part of the change that’s needed as the country recovers from deadly earthquakes and tries to restructure a mountain of debt after years of mismanagement. Respected former central bank president Ruth Krivoy and leading oil executive Ali Moshiri of Amos Global Energy give their takes on the role oil can play. Meanwhile, the president of Venezuela’s Chambers of Commerce and Industry, Felipe Capozzolo of Fedecamaras, explains some of the other reforms that could help the country become wealthy again.

programme.title: Such Brave Girls
programme.desc: Deb invites new boyfriend Dev home to meet her daughters Billie and Josie whilst desperately trying to suppress how troubled they are. Josie’s face isn’t doing a very good job of covering up how depressed she is, so Deb sets out to teach her how fulfilling capitalism can be by taking her shopping. Billie spots the love of her life, Nicky, with a new girl, so decides to win him back with a significant change to her appearance and discovers just how much love hurts.

programme.title: Such Brave Girls
programme.desc: Despite enjoying his stoic silence, Deb’s starting to worry that she and Dev might have nothing to talk about. She’s determined to find something in common through any means necessary. Billie is worried that Nicky might be pulling away from her so decides to play hard to get. Josie is trying to impress the girl at the bar, but her relentlessly loving and wormy boyfriend Seb has just found out she’s back and is keen to get things back to how they used to be.

programme.title: Such Brave Girls
programme.desc: The pressure is on for Josie - she is determined to make her birthday dinner last as long as possible so she doesn’t have to come good on a deal made with boyfriend Seb. Deb thinks she’s really getting through to Dev’s wallet, and maybe this time he’s going to step up and finally pay for something - especially considering he’s the one who suggested they all go for dinner.

programme.title: Such Brave Girls
programme.desc: As Billie and Josie’s imminent breakdowns loom, Deb tries to pretend everything’s fine with a big trip to the woods... but she’s mainly there to prove she’s just as outdoorsy as Dev’s wife used to be. In an attempt to prove she’s more than her trauma and because she’s got 'loads' of pain, Josie decides she’s an artist, which upsets everyone. She doesn’t let her lack of inspiration or discernible talent stop her. Billie welcomes a new man into her life, and takes on the big questions, like if God is good, why is there evil in the world? And if God made nature, why is it so relentlessly boring?

programme.title: Such Brave Girls
programme.desc: Over one long night, Deb, Billie and Josie find their own ways to process death after visiting their nan in hospital. Josie starts to wonder whether her own pathetic life might be half-lived, and Billie tries to find their dad. Billie and Josie attempt to cope with their profound existential despair by going clubbing, where Billie befriends her rival, and Josie finally works out who she is. Back at home, Dev’s got a bee in his bonnet about sending the girls to therapy, and Deb is on a mission to prove therapy is useless. Seb starts to panic that Josie might be kissing a girl.

programme.title: Such Brave Girls
programme.desc: Preparing to see their dad again, Josie writes a speech to tell him how she feels, and Billie’s got newfound confidence that all men eventually come crawling back. Dev is gutted he’s not invited to a family funeral and has a very big question for Deb. With a fresh swagger, Josie’s breakdown is welcome news for Seb, who can’t wait to spend the rest of his life with her. Lunch at Dev’s house goes to waste as it’s abandoned for a rescue mission, and, worst of all, Deb might be forced to come clean about her lie.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi is rightfully asked if she’s ‘thick’ for bothering an electrician working on an out-of-order lift. For once in her life, Chi is forced to reconcile with her own intelligence. At her weekly grief counselling sessions, Ruth doesn’t exactly hold back, telling Chi she is indeed simple and not to bother seeking adult education. Chi sets out to prove her wrong and breaks into Ramsgate College in search of an education.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi’s ghost parents tell her she should really be worried about dying alone and encourage her to find a life partner. Chi casts a very wide and desperate net for potential love interests, approaching almost everyone in Ramsgate with her phone number. Meanwhile, Lucas gets a job at the cinema but is crumbling under the pressure and the perfectly normal expectations of his manager, Kenneth. Lucas resorts to stress-eating the pick ’n’ mix when nobody is looking.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: It’s Chi’s last free therapy session, and Ruth wants to know whether Chi can still see her dead parents or whether she’s learned anything at all from the counselling. But she very much can still see her dead parents; in fact, they were just in the hallway, wearing outdoor clothes and discussing what will become of them if they leave the house. Will they pass on to another plane? Will this be the end of them?

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: The BBC's biggest comedy talent search is celebrating its 30th birthday, and we're heading to Bristol, where five comics will compete in the first of six knockout heats.

programme.title: BBC New Comedy Awards
programme.desc: Birmingham’s Hockley Social Club has been transformed into our very own comedy club. Taking to the stage are Eli Hart, Farhan Solo, Chloe Reynolds, Will BF and Monica Hsueh in a bid to impress our judges and book their place in the final. Award-winning comedian and writer Sarah Keyworth is here to keep the house in order. The judges are comedian, writer and podcaster Aurie Styla and local Brum stand-up Lindsey Santoro. Head judge Fatiha El-Ghorri completes the trio. It’s not going to be easy for them to pick a winner from the five new comics performing. With only five minutes on stage each, the sets are jam-packed with jokes and cutting-edge material, but only one can go through to the grand final in November at City of Culture 25 Bradford’s Alhambra Theatre.

programme.desc: Programmes start at 7.00pm

programme.desc: Programmes start at 7.00pm

programme.title: This is BBC Three
programme.desc: Programmes start at 7.00pm

programme.title: The Catch Up
programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve and the team embark on a truly incredible adventure across the vast island of Madagascar. Many of the creatures they meet cannot be found anywhere else in the world. From gremlin-like aye-ayes to Madagascar's most ferocious carnivore, Steve has some unique encounters as he searches for contenders for the Deadly 60.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve is in Uganda, getting up close and personal with some of our closest relatives - the primates. He meets gorillas in the mountains and squabbling baboons on the savannah. He even has a dawn encounter with chimps in the forest.

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The ten remaining sewers celebrate the rich fashion and textile traditions of Mexico. Host Sophie Willan and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young are joined by a special guest judge, renowned fashion designer Erika Alvirez. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers create a Mexican folkloric top using fabrics created by indigenous communities in Mexico’s Oaxaca region. For the Transformation Challenge, they are given manteles de hule, a traditional Mexican tablecloth. Using the stiffness of the fabric, they are asked to create a garment with an eye-catching structure. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers design an outfit inspired by one of the many Mexican festivals found across the country.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May are on a mission to build a bridge over the River Kwai in Thailand. However, in order to do that they must first drive across a country that has been largely closed to westerners for over 40 years: Burma. Furthermore, the trio must make this trip in three lorries that have been bought 'sight unseen' from the internet for a limited budget. Unsurprisingly, they are not quite as the trio might have hoped or expected. What follows is an epic journey of beautiful scenery, regular adversity, ongoing malfunction and the constant bickering of three badly dressed buffoons.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson, Richard Hammond and James May are battling across Burma in three ancient and barely functioning lorries. Having forded rivers, climbed mountains and endured a Burmese trucker stop, they must now venture into the Shan state, an area rife with civil war and normally closed to western TV crews, as they head towards Thailand and their final challenge - to build a bridge over the River Kwai.

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: It is Tommy’s birthday, but there is no time for cake. With just days to go before his long-awaited comeback fight in Budapest, Tommy is pulled in every direction, juggling press conferences, promo shoots and the pressure of proving he has still got what it takes in the ring. Fighting on the same bill as his older brother Roman, Tommy steps into the spotlight once again and puts himself to the test against a hard-hitting Bosnian heavyweight. In a high-stakes bout that could define his future, Tommy isn’t just fighting for his career - he is fighting for the life he is desperate to rebuild. Meanwhile, there is a more personal battle quietly playing out at home. With the house freshly prepared for Molly-Mae and Bambi’s return, Tommy hopes he has done enough to prove he has changed. But now that he may have won them back, can he keep them?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: After the success of his comeback fight, Tommy’s road to redemption hits a major setback - his hand is injured again and needs eight weeks’ total rest before doctors will know if he can fight again. The last time he couldn’t train, his life spiralled out of control, so now Tommy throws himself into a frenzy of activity: a TV appearance on The Wheel, family days out with Bambi, and a final push to finish the home he hopes Molly and Bambi will soon return to. In search of focus and inspiration, Tommy heads to Marbella to train with his childhood hero - legendary bodybuilder Dorian Yates. But in a world of yacht trips, sun-soaked distractions and luxury villas, can Tommy stay disciplined and keep his relationship and boxing career back on track? As doubts grow over his recovery, Tommy faces the toughest question of all - is this just a setback or the beginning of the end of his boxing career?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy’s recovery is back on track after he and John put his hand to the test. The pair are training again, and the search for Tommy’s next opponent begins. Eager to make the most of family time, Tommy splashes out on a £90,000 motor home for family trips with Molly and Bambi and takes his mum out for lunch and a long-overdue catch-up. Tommy reveals that John has had a recent health scare, so to cheer him up, father and son take their very different caravans to a local steam fair. It’s vital for Tommy’s mental health that he keeps physically active at all times, so he sets his sights on an ambitious new goal - a 100km triathlon. Meanwhile, John worries that the physical toll from this could jeopardise the chances of Tommy recovering and landing a big money fight. As Tommy throws himself into training for the triathlon, one question remains - can he avoid getting injured, or will this new challenge end his boxing career for good?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy realises just how far he and Molly have come since their separation last year, but John’s worries grow as Tommy takes on a 100km triathlon, pushing his body to new physical limits. Before the challenge, Tommy takes some downtime at the spa with his mates, preparing for a huge press push ahead of his series premiere. He’s come a long way since he and Molly separated last year, and the truth hits home when he sees his face on a billboard - and shares the moment with Molly. The premiere brings together family and friends, all celebrating how far Tommy has come. But there’s no time to rest - he heads to the south of France for the triathlon, where Molly and Bambi surprise him at the finishing line. Even with the triathlon behind him, Tommy’s pursuit of physical challenges continues as he gears up for the Great North Run the following week. Riding a high, he is suddenly hit with a backlash on social media, leaving him to wonder what he can do to catch a break.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: When running a big school, how much discipline is too much? Panorama investigates the academy trust where classrooms are silent and pupils can be sent to detention for looking out of the window. For some, reduced disruption and improved exam results at schools run by the Athena Learning Trust in Devon and Cornwall is proof that the tough approach works. But as Richard Bilton reports, many former teachers, students and their parents say the trust’s strict policies on behaviour have gone too far.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Gabs and Dick uncover evidence that Leonard is hiding something, while floods in India match Bethany’s drawings. Gabs pushes her suspicions into the open.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Brinicle tries to turn the Krispy Krill shack into a top restaurant to impress a secret reviewer, but chef Pancake’s cooking proves unpopular, and Looph’s plate machine misfires.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Whilst playing doctors, Cosima discovers an animal with no heartbeat! Can Cosima and Big Lizard save the poor creature with Dad's medical kit?

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings get creative and make sculptures of themselves out of straw. Weasy thinks he can do better, but his sculpture is a fiasco. The Farm of the Future offers a precise cutting system. Will Weasy be able to outsmart his daughters?

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Blossom draws the short cheese straw and, rather than join her friends on a picnic, she has to take a magic wand to the recycling centre. Faced with a long queue and a rumbly tummy, Blossom decides that life is too short for recycling - with disastrous consequences. The heroes must skip their picnic and go on a quest to save the forest from the magical mess Blossom has gotten them into.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: Grizzy finds a polar bear and realises they are from the same species.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: When Duck and Frog work on a farm, Frog makes the perfect scarecrow. However, he gets covered in super-strong fertiliser and becomes a giant, monster-sized, chaos-causing Frog!

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Amethio meets Mighty G, and a surfing Gholdengo wows the Rising Volt Tacklers.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: A dark spell transforms Bloom into Dark Bloom, turning her against her friends and wreaking havoc at Alfea. Meanwhile, Aisha's love of dance clashes with her parents' expectations.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Jamie Johnson FC
programme.desc: It’s all change at Hawx Academy as former Foxborough player Charlie must prove herself to her teammates, their new coach and an all-access documentary crew.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Frances Tophill returns to Damson Farm in Bath and spends the day with owner Alison and a very special guest – Dame Mary Berry. Returning to the city where she grew up and went to school, Mary shares how the landscapes and countryside around Bath nurtured a lifelong love of gardening and the great outdoors. Together, they share practical gardening advice and celebrate the very best of summer, harvesting homegrown fruit, vegetables and flowers at their seasonal peak. Frances has advice on how to create a wild corner that's both beautiful and beneficial for wildlife while collecting seeds for future displays. Arit Anderson visits an inspiring urban edible garden in London, and there's a city gardener transforming a compact space into a thriving haven for wildlife. Toby Buckland shares clever ways to extend the growing season and make the most of summer harvests, and in Birmingham, there's a visit to a predominantly Punjabi allotment community where growing exceptional produce is intertwined with family, culture and tradition, creating plots that are as productive as they are beautiful.

programme.title: Angels One Five
programme.desc: Second World War drama relating the Battle of Britain through the eyes of the operations room of a Kent fighter station during the summer of 1940. A young, inexperienced pilot has trouble settling into the routine of squadron life, and his adherence to the rule book puts him out of favour with his comrades. Can he win them round?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: The ten remaining sewers celebrate the rich fashion and textile traditions of Mexico. Host Sophie Willan and judges Patrick Grant and Esme Young are joined by a special guest judge, renowned fashion designer Erika Alvirez. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers create a Mexican folkloric top using fabrics created by indigenous communities in Mexico’s Oaxaca region. For the Transformation Challenge, they are given manteles de hule, a traditional Mexican tablecloth. Using the stiffness of the fabric, they are asked to create a garment with an eye-catching structure. Finally, in the Made-to-Measure, the sewers design an outfit inspired by one of the many Mexican festivals found across the country.

programme.title: A Cook Abroad
programme.desc: MasterChef judge Monica Galetti steps outside her comfort zone as she swaps her chef's whites for wellies and heads for the Jura Mountains in eastern France to get hands-on with the produce she uses every day in the London restaurant where she works. Monica embarks on a road trip through one of the most beautiful yet least known regions in France, where, for the first time in her cooking career, she spends time with producers. She sees for herself how their passion translates into world-class ingredients. Immersing herself in a traditional way of life, she joins a boar hunt and faces up to the responsibility of eating meat. From beauty contests for cows to cutting down trees, she unlocks the secret to making some of our favourite French cheeses and discovers an ancient profession she never knew existed. Finally, on the slopes of Mont d'Or, Monica cooks up a rustic feast using ingredients she's gathered herself, fulfilling a personal ambition to live off the land.

programme.title: Summer Holiday
programme.desc: Don and his friends persuade their employer to lend them a London bus for their summer holiday. En route to the south of France, the boys run into some girls and offer them a lift to Athens. Then, they pick up an American boy who isn't exactly what he seems but who is running away from an exploitative mother.

programme.title: Fake or Fortune?
programme.desc: Our art sleuths investigate 15 prints found in a garage, each potentially worth thousands. Are they really by notorious 20th-century artist Lucian Freud? Or just crafty fakes?

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the dolphin get so smart? Chris Packham dives into one of the biggest questions in nature - how intelligence itself evolved and how it arose in the extraordinary mind of the dolphin. Inside each one lies the result of a three-billion-year journey, from light-sensing cells to conscious thought.

programme.title: Superman II
programme.desc: Three Kryptonian criminals who share Superman’s extraordinary powers arrive on Earth with the intent of conquering it. Superman must use all his strength and intelligence to outwit them.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Nick Mohammed journeys through the Proms archive to celebrate the music that transformed people's view of the universe. Featuring Richard Strauss's Also sprach Zarathustra from 2001: A Space Odyssey, Gustav Holst's The Planets, John Williams's scores for Star Wars and E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Hans Zimmer's Interstellar and Max Richter's On the Nature of Daylight, heard in Arrival. Prepare for a journey from the concert hall to galaxies far, far away.

programme.title: Paul Heaton at the BBC
programme.desc: One of Britain’s most prolific and successful singer-songwriters of the past four decades, Paul Heaton started his career as frontman of The Housemartins before forming The Beautiful South, the band of whom it was famously once claimed that one in seven UK households owns an album. Whether that's true or not, what is a fact is that Paul has demonstrated over the years a unique ability to write songs and lyrics that have fans weeping one moment and smiling the next. This collection of performances and best BBC moments celebrates Paul’s impressive career - the bands, the collaborations and the solo work - and features the man himself explaining the context and backstories behind some of his best-loved hits. From The Housemartins’ debut release Sheep through to Fish 'N' Chip Supper from his solo album The Mighty Several and a triumphant appearance at Glastonbury 2024 that featured a glorious reunion with Norman ‘Fatboy Slim’ Cook, it’s a celebration that can definitely guarantee viewers a Happy Hour (and a half).

programme.title: Paul Heaton: Live at Bramall Lane
programme.desc: Paul Heaton takes to the stage at Sheffield's iconic Bramall Lane for a landmark concert. Recorded live in 2025, this unforgettable performance showcases one of Britain's most admired songwriters with songs spanning more than four decades, from the timeless classics of The Housemartins and The Beautiful South to highlights from his solo career. Backed by his stellar live band, including regular singing partner Rianne Downey, Paul Heaton delivers a set filled with wit, warmth and unmistakable melodies, performing beloved favourites alongside newer material for an audience at his beloved Sheffield United Football Club.

programme.title: The Housemartins in London 0 Hull 4
programme.desc: The Housemartins wake up one morning to discover that suddenly they're the fourth-best band in Hull. This intimate documentary is a unique record of the early days, looking at how a meteoric rise to fame left their home lives irrevocably unchanged. First broadcast 1987.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: A compilation of Top of the Pops performances from The Beautiful South.

programme.title: Fallen Leaves
programme.desc: Comedy romance set in modern-day Helsinki. A lonely metalworker and a single woman working as a supermarket shelf stacker meet by chance in a karaoke bar. Drawn to each other, they strike a quiet yet immediate connection. Along their uneven path to happiness lie lost phone numbers, mistaken addresses, alcoholism and a charming stray dog. Aki Kaurismäki's Nordic comedy romance, winner of the Cannes Festival Jury Prize. In Finnish with English subtitles.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Gabs finally meets Anika Drake. New nurse Siobhan raises suspicions at Oxsmith. When Bethany is found injured, Gabs and Rafiq plan her escape. Max pushes Caroline to back Rostyre.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The A to Z of TV Gardening
programme.desc: Carol Kirkwood takes an alphabetical journey through the world of gardening, getting inspiration and advice from some of the BBC's most popular garden presenters and programmes. In this episode, she's exploring subjects that all begin with the letter R. Programmes include Gardeners' World, Flying Gardener, RHS Chelsea Flower Show and Countryfile. With presenters Toby Buckland, Rachel de Thame, Monty Don, Julia Bradbury, Chris Beardshaw, Alan Titchmarsh and Joe Swift.

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Christine Walkden's balloon travels over the flattest part of Britain as she descends on Norfolk. At East Ruston Gardens she helps cut a hole in a hedge and meets Kathryn, a very determined woman. At the Bressingham Gardens, Christine assists in preparing a tree for felling and we discover the fascinating human history of the Norfolk Broads.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In the first of four special episodes, Adam Henson meets a new generation of farmers navigating the challenges and opportunities of producing our food. Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. Adam joins her on the daily rounds to discover the realities of running a traditional hill farm and hears how she is balancing the responsibility of carrying on a family legacy with the need to build a resilient business for the future. Adam also looks back through the show's archives at some of the inspirational young farmers we have met across the UK.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek explores three well-known castles as he revisits his favourite heritage walks. They include Powys Castle, the spooky Margam Castle and the medieval Kidwelly Castle.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Brian Cunningham’s beginner’s guide to vegetable growing started in April, and now it’s time to reap the rewards as he starts to harvest from the veg plot at Beechgrove Garden. Calum Clunie sows for winter crops as he starts the sowing cycle again on his family-sized plo. He also refreshes the containers he started in April as a demonstration of just what you can do if space is limited and you only room for some pots. Brian and Calum tackle Beechgrove’s hedges after checking carefully for bird nest activity, and Brian advises on caring for common houseplants. There is a visit to St Andrews Botanic Garden, along with the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Rosie Birkett celebrates the best of summer salads with her bavette carpaccio, fried capers and a tangy mustard dressing, all served alongside a refreshing panzanella. Mike Reid kicks off the BBQ vibes indoors with his mango-marinated spatchcock chicken, fiery kiwi hot sauce and a bitter radicchio and pear salad. The former head chef at the Italian embassy, Danilo Cortellini, serves up a multicoloured ricotta-stuffed ravioli dressed in basil and tomato sauce. Jez Rose heads to a very soggy Leicestershire to get picking, prepping and packing a classic elderflower cordial. Genevieve Taylor continues the barbecue theme by demonstrating how to master fish on the grill with leek-wrapped cod and almond saffron sauce. And finally, Oti Mabuse faces her food heaven or food hell. Meanwhile, Rick Stein rustles up a classic Italian dish in his Cornish kitchen, and Si and Dave make their way towards a fusion feast in Newport.

programme.title: Indian Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Anjum Anand heads off to Cornwall to meet self-taught chefs Nirmal and Louis who run the The Little Cornish Curry Company. Originally from Birmingham, for the last few years they have been serving up curry at the farmers markets near where they live as well as catering for the odd event. But now they are about to face a new test. Local pub The Galleon Inn is launching a curry night with Louis and Nirmal doing the food. They have decided that the best way to convert the customers to Indian food is to start with a regional favourite - fish. However Louis and Nirmal haven't used fish in Indian food much, so first up Anjum takes them to famous Looe fish market where the fish is officially the freshest in Britain. Having chosen some fantastic Pollock, Anjum shows them how to make a rich, flavoursome South Indian coconut fish curry with a side order of yellow lemon rice and crab cakes garnished with tangy tamarind mayonnaise.

programme.title: Indian Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Anjum Anand sees how well all the people in the previous episodes have got on with their new found cooking skills by holding a party in her garden. The catch - they all have to make an Indian dish for the others to try. First of all Anjum must prepare her contribution - a glorious spiced roast leg of lamb, commonly known in India as a raan. To get the best meat available she visits a top Halal butchers in South London, and gets to know her goat from her lamb. Then she starts to re-visit her Indian food novices: good friend Alex is going to cook a classic side dish of paneer with spinach; glamorous Panthea is going to try her hand at a creamy raita; head chef Elisha from the health spa is going to whip up a fabulous mushroom pilaff, and Paul the firefighter is going to try and get to grips with peshwari naan. With the sun finally coming out, and cocktail expert Ben Reed getting the party-goers in the mood, it is time for Anjum and the guests to see how they've all got on.

programme.title: The Man Who Knew Too Much
programme.desc: Dr and Mrs McKenna's holiday in North Africa is interrupted when a passing acquaintance dies and they learn their son has been kidnapped.

programme.title: Cricket: The Hundred
programme.desc: Coverage of The Hundred 100-ball cricket tournament in the women's game.

programme.title: Cricket: The Hundred
programme.desc: Coverage of The Hundred 100-ball cricket tournament in the men's game.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: The magnificent Lou Sanders introduces comedians Celya AB and Neil Delamere to the stage.

programme.title: Inside Llewyn Davis
programme.desc: A week in the life of Llewyn Davis, a struggling folk singer in 1961 New York. Penniless, homeless and sleeping on the couches of friends, he is hoping for his big break in the music industry.

programme.title: Lady Macbeth
programme.desc: Newly married to a rich industrialist, Katherine finds herself confined to the house and starved of companionship. Forced to spend her days in endless tedium when her husband is called away to one of his collieries, she begins a passionate and fiery relationship with a young groom from the estate, beginning a conflict with her stern and unforgiving family that will end in tragedy.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Sue has invited Michael and Renee to a nice family dinner in an attempt to play happy families, which means she can’t accept Phyllis’s invite to her surprise birthday party. Michael and Renee’s real motive for coming round is revealed, and things take a turn for the worst. Fortunately, Linda is there to avert tragedy and reveal the biggest shock of the night.

programme.title: The Devil in the Family: The Fall of Ruby Franke
programme.desc: With the family increasingly isolated, the home begins to draw unwanted attention. When a lucky escape exposes Ruby and Jodi’s world, the truth proves far worse than anyone imagined.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Danny visits The One Show studio, where Alex Jones and Roman Kemp reveal their love of antiques and collectibles. In Builth Wells, two teams of well-known faces search for bargains.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Kev's in hot water! Boiling, in fact, as he wrestles with a rusty water tank. Upholsterer Larissa needs to find a way of getting a tired set of dining chairs sitting pretty again. And Jacqui Joseph takes on her biggest challenge to date, a massive display unit, but will she manage to make it fit for a modern home?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc: It’s a family affair as Steve Fletcher fixes a model watermill while son Fred brings a cherished clock back to life. The team also fix a stunning Notting Hill Carnival headpiece.

Margie's keen to do it again, while Tim is playing for pride, pleasure and, of course, profits. They start out in Blackpool, and this time the wheels will be an electric-powered 1970 crew cab fire engine. Can they set the saleroom ablaze when they go head-to-head?

Meanwhile, Charlie visits a family firm in Llangollen who are crafting wood to make standing frames for people with spinal injuries.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Mehreen Baig, Clare Balding, Jamie Laing and Mike Wozniak take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay is at the helm of this quiz all about the UK. The Traitors star Paul Gorton leads an unreliable tour of a different destination each day, with celebrity players battling it out to sort unbelievable facts from fiction. This week’s guests are EastEnders star Nitin Ganatra, the Reverend Kate Bottley and Gladiator Apollo, aka Alex Gray. The tour starts in Derry/Londonderry. A daily winner is declared at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned.

programme.title: The Farmers' Country Showdown
programme.desc: Livestock farmer Lyn is proud that her sons, Thomas and Jack, have inherited her passion for rearing and promoting rare-breed animals. It means running their North Yorkshire farm is a family effort. However, they are all preparing for stiff competition against each other at the Staffordshire County Show. With their own different rare-breed flocks, Jack has high hopes that he will beat his mum in the show ring when his spiralled-horned Boreray meets her four-horned Manx Loaghtan. Meanwhile, Jersey cattle farming couple Jan and David, and his daughter Fiona, are just as determined to bag themselves a row of rosettes for their Shropshire farm. David has competed at the Staffordshire County Show for nearly 40 years and is confident he knows how to become a champion. They have each picked their favourite cow and will all go head-to-head in the show ring. However, Fiona’s got a job on her hands dealing with her grumpy Jersey.

programme.title: Spy in the Ocean
programme.desc: Spy creatures reveal an ocean full of startling ways of thinking, including the largest brain, smart octopi, diving monkeys, creative masterminds and other intriguing intelligence.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the experts visit the gardens of Chartwell in Kent, the former home of Sir Winston Churchill, where they are shown a painting by Graham Sutherland found behind a water tank. There is also a Gainsborough portrait, a collection of signatures by Battle of Britain pilots stationed at Biggin Hill, and a Russian sub-machine gun owned by a vicar.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin revisits some of the locations visited by Flog It! and presents all-new valuations. Experts touch down at Bletchley Park, the Ulster Transport Museum and Crowcombe Court to track down some unusual items to sell at auction. They uncover a beautiful watercolour and some stunning porcelain, and Paul Martin visits Antony in Cornwall to unearth a fascinating family history.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games

Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Former best friends Rhys and Niall come together in the wild to see if they can repair their relationship after barely speaking for the last two years. Their friendship faltered after the death of Niall’s older brother, when grief left him feeling withdrawn from those around him, and Rhys was unsure how best to reach out. The pair are set a canoeing challenge, and side by side, they also take on a forward-facing abseil down a sheer cliff face. In a campfire chat with mediator Mo, the pair talk for the first time about the reasons they drifted apart, confront past hurts and share the pain of bereavement. Will these two days be enough to rebuild the trust and friendship they once shared?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: Five gold medals will be awarded in the first evening session of the European Athletics Championships as the women’s shot put final gets underway. There’s also qualifying for the women’s 100m hurdles. This is the first time that Great Britain has ever hosted these Championships, and there are over 1,600 athletes from 48 countries taking part. Gabby Logan is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford, and they reflect on all the action from the morning session as well as previewing the women’s 100m final. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Victoria Coren Mitchell hosts the quiz where knowledge only gets you so far – the vital extra ingredients are logic and lateral thinking. Three Rocky Horror fans take on a team of New Zealanders, trying to establish the connection between such clues as back save, leg help, face accept the reality and knees party. One of the teams worked it out after three clues – but what is the answer?

programme.title: Evolution

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul and Bob venture from London to the Scottish Highlands, taking a sleeper train overnight to their destination. They wake in the stunning vista of north west Scotland, where the pine forests and snow-topped mountains almost take their breath away. They are on a quest to fish for ferox trout, which is a tall order for any angler. But they are in the right place, the River Garry, with a local guide to help them target their quarry. Setting off in a boat, the pair fish long and hard, while also taking time to look for the Loch Ness monster.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In the first of four special episodes, Adam Henson meets a new generation of farmers navigating the challenges and opportunities of producing our food. Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. Adam joins her on the daily rounds to discover the realities of running a traditional hill farm and hears how she is balancing the responsibility of carrying on a family legacy with the need to build a resilient business for the future. Adam also looks back through the show's archives at some of the inspirational young farmers we have met across the UK.
